---
title: "The critical friend"
description: "You give independent advice on one piece of work. What you are confirming, how far apart you have to be, and what happens to what you find."
---

{{< include /guidance/_partials/role-critical-friend.qmd >}}

## What you are confirming

Three things, and they are narrower than a general opinion of the work.

- That **appropriate and sufficient quality assurance has taken place** for the level the work is at.
- That the **use of the outputs is appropriate**, which means the results can carry the decision
  they are about to be used for.
- That the **assumptions and risks are understood**, by you and by the people relying on the work.

You are giving advice. The commissioner owns the decision, and the analyst owns the analysis.

## Your part in each phase

| Phase | What is yours |
|---|---|
| [Phase 1. Engagement and scoping](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) | Understand the brief |
| [Phase 2. Design](../02-design/index.qmd) | Review the plan, confirm you can do the assurance the level asks for, and put your own time in the schedule |
| [Phase 3. Analysis](../03-analysis/index.qmd) | Run the checks the level requires, and report back |
| [Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd) | State what you assured |
| [Phase 5. Review](../05-review/index.qmd) | What you found is what the next piece of work avoids |

## How independent you have to be

**The assurer and the analyst shall be independent.** What varies is how far apart.

| Level | The reviewer is |
|---|---|
| Level 1 Standard | A colleague, within your team |
| Level 2 Enhanced | Someone who had no hand in producing the work |
| Level 3 Comprehensive | An assurer from outside the delivering team |
| Level 4 BCA | A Lead Assurer from outside the delivering team, with external review |

There is no level at which nobody independent looks at the work, and none at which the analyst is
excused their own checks. Theirs are the first line, not the last one.

Beyond any one assignment, assurance sits on three defined levels: operational management, senior
management independent of it, and independent bodies. Analysis should be peer reviewed by
independent individuals or groups.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-independence-distance.qmd >}}

## Which checks the level asks of you

What you run is set by the assurance level, not by how much time you have.
[The checks, by level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd#the-checks-by-level) lists
them. Where there is not enough time for the assurance the level requires, say so plainly rather
than absorb it. [When you disagree](index.qmd#when-you-disagree) sets out where that goes.
